summary: Flame in Freefall is an interactive dashboard that summarizes, ranks and interprets NASA PSI microgravity combustion investigations for crew fire safety. It has four pages: a catalog with side-by-side comparison; a mission-relevance ranking (ISS, Moon base, pressurized rover, Mars habitat) with adjustable, transparent weights; a coverage map of tested oxygen and pressure conditions against the Moon-base target zone (O2 >= 30 %, <= 70.3 kPa); and an AI assistant that answers only from the catalog. Of 1,138 test rows, 813 were verified cell by cell against the NASA PSI tables; the rest are labelled "not yet verified". Key finding: 48 verified tests fall in the Moon-base zone, all with gaseous fuels (ACME CFI-G). Solid-fuel tests (BASS-II) reached only 22.2 % O2, and fire-suppression tests (FLEX) have none in the zone. BASS-II pressure is an assumption (ISS cabin, about 1 atm). Data: NASA PSI (CC0).
details:
Flame in Freefall is a Streamlit dashboard that turns NASA PSI microgravity combustion data into fire-safety insight for crews. Four pages: (1) Catalog: 24 PSI investigations with side-by-side comparison; (2) Ranking: relevance for ISS, Moon base, pressurized rover and Mars habitat, with adjustable, transparent weights and a plain-language reason for every score; (3) Coverage Map: every tested condition (O2 % vs pressure kPa) against the Moon-base target zone (O2 >= 30 %, <= 70.3 kPa), showing the gaps; (4) AI Assistant: answers only from the catalog, cites the investigation, and says "Not in the data" otherwise.

Data: 1,138 test rows from PSI tables (ACME CFI-G, ACME Flame Design, FLEX, CFI, BASS-II). 813 rows were checked cell by cell against the tables on psi.nasa.gov; the rest are labelled "not yet verified". BASS-II tables have no pressure column, so its pressure is a labelled assumption (ISS cabin, about 1 atm).

Key finding: 48 verified tests fall inside the Moon-base zone, all with gaseous fuels (ACME CFI-G). Solid-fuel tests (BASS-II) reached only 22.2 % O2, and fire-suppression tests (FLEX) have none in the zone.

Tools: Python, pandas, Streamlit, Google Gemini API (assistant), GitHub.

SI use: Claude (Anthropic) helped write the data-conversion, validation and scoring code and draft text; Gemini powers the in-app assistant. Data values were taken from NASA PSI tables and verified against them; no images or video were SI-generated.
